title: Best way to get 2D assets + animations (like idle breathing and etc) in pixel style for IOS app if you're not an artist, with AI tool ?
author: 0full1stack01
selftext:
I'm a VibeCoder and am developing an iOS app.

I need an AI tool that can generate 2D pixel-style assets with animations, which I can then integrate into my app.

**I would appreciate any help.**

comments.body: I got you I’ve been building a platform for this exact reason send me a DM

comments.author: teamharder
comments.body: Ludo is solid. I built a schmup game with generated sprite from there plus animations for idle and explosions.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
So the main issue with using something like Nano Banana or GPT image gen for spritesheets is that those models can't output transparency, and they have no concept of animation frames. You'll spend more time cleaning up the output than you saved generating it.

https://i.redd.it/693wcnv9d64h1.gif

I actually ran into this enough that I ended up building GameLab Studio [https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co) . It handles transparent spritesheets, consistent angles/palette across frames, and tileable textures. Not perfect for everything but it's been solid for prototyping and even some production stuff.

For integration, export your spritesheets and use something like SpriteKit or Lottie on the iOS side to play them back.

replies.author: adam_goodman
replies.body: This seems like a really great tool.  I'll definitely be a customer if it ends up as seamless as it appears in the first pass.  Not sure how I would go about rotating an existing sprite sheet I made into all 8 directions though?

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Hi Adam,

I’m glad you found Gamelabs Studio helpful. It’s a pretty seamless experience to generate the other orientations. If you’re using the wizard, there should be a “next orientation” button on the last page once you’ve created the spritesheet, that will take you back to the select orientation page. Just choose the next orientation you want to make, and then when you go to the image page, use the dropdown menu to select the initial image you generated, the first time, to use as your reference image.

If you’re in the Freeform view, simply change the orientation in the dropdown menus at the top of the page, and then in the image dialog, select the first one you generated as the reference from the dropdown menu.

All the orientations are stored in the asset, and show up with a green dot next to the ones you have already generated in the menu. In Freeform view you can see the thumbnails for all the orientations you have already generated, along the top toolbar as well as
